County.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock.

* WHEN...Until this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Minor lowland flooding extends
into low areas of the flood plain with no significant impact.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CST Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM CST Wednesday was 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 3.5 feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.2
feet on 08/31/2022.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 945 AM CST.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:49AM EST until November 15 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Deland to remain
just below Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain nearly
steady into next week, but may slowly climb into Minor flood stage
this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
early Friday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL SUNDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:46AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in continued
river levels in Minor Flood Stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady into the weekend as a large volume of water works north
through the basin, though developing northerly winds could generate a
small rise.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Wednesday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte and Northern Coastal Humboldt

* WHEN...From 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late Saturday
through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday
through Monday.
properties.instruction:

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

expected.

Island Hawaii.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Thursday.

branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.

sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

properties.areaDesc: Baraga; Marquette
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 11 at 7:07AM EST until November 13 at 12:00PM EST by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
...ACCUMULATING LAKE EFFECT SNOW TONIGHT THROUGH FRIDAY...

.Lake effect rain showers transition to snow this evening and
continue through Friday. Wet snow accumulations are expected away
from the Lake Superior shoreline with several inches of snowfall over
the higher terrain.

* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Total snow accumulations between
4 and 8 inches over the higher elevations of Marquette County and
Baraga County with locally up to 10 inches. Less than an inch of
snowfall is expected near the Lake Superior shoreline. Winds
gusting as high as 30 mph and up to 40 mph near Lake Superior.

* WHERE...Baraga and Marquette Counties.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to noon EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday morning and evening commutes along with
the Friday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lake effect rain showers will transition to
all snow this evening. Warmer temperatures near Lake Superior will
limit accumulations to less than an inch near the lakeshore,
including the city of Marquette. Conditions will deteriorate
rapidly as you move inland, particularly US-41 between Marquette
and Negaunee. Some improvement to travel is expected Thursday
afternoon as temperatures warm to near or slightly above freezing,
with deteriorating conditions again Thursday evening, around
sunset.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 3:39AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Observed flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics has ended, but flooding on the
Skokomish River will continue into late this morning as the flood
crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 AM PST Wednesday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage midday
and continue falling to near 15.0 feet late tonight.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6
feet on 10/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon PST.

move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 11 at 12:14AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 30
ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM Friday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, from 9 PM Wednesday through 6 PM
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 10 at 8:13PM PST until November 16 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip
currents. These waves are expected to significantly increase
Friday into the weekend. Minor tidal overflows are possible
during morning high tides.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. There is
potential for warning-level surf, significant beach erosion
and enhanced coastal flooding risk. Posing most risk to west-
facing beaches. Coastal hazards are likely to continue well
into next week.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Brooks, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 10 at 4:42PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Latest observations show that Low Olmos Creek near Falfurrias has
risen to Action Stage (5.0 feet) with a current level of 6.21 feet.
Levels are expected to remain above Action Stage through tonight and
likely through Wednesday (at least).

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 6.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.7 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CST.

properties.areaDesc: Los Angeles County Beaches; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 10 at 12:18PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne and
Manhattan Beach. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT DUE TO HARMFUL FINE PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 1:15PM CST until November 11 at 5:20PM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Llano River at Llano affecting Llano County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Llano River at Llano.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding makes secondary
roads and low bridges in the flood plain dangerous to motorists
including the low water crossing of Ranch Road 3404/Slab Road near
Kingsland. Equipment should be moved from low docks and boat ties
loosened downstream in Kingsland.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 14.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:00 PM CST Tuesday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tonight and continue falling to 3.8 feet early Sunday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.6
feet on 06/01/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 115 AM CST.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 10 at 11:14AM PST until November 16 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to a foot, with up to 2 feet at the highest peaks.
Minor accumulations of around an 1 inch possible down to 5000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108. Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening and Monday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause downed tree branches and localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 7000 to 8000 feet Friday, lowering
to 6500 feet Saturday, then down to around 5000 feet by Monday
morning. Heaviest snowfall expected Friday night into Saturday
morning. Light flurries to a dusting possible down to 5000 feet
with measurable accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. There
could be a break during the day Saturday, followed by additional
snow Saturday night into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.
